LESSON: READING 4.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: CLASS READERS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.4: Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: how the main characters make the story flow. 1. How can you tell the main character in a story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the main characters in a class reader,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explain how the characters make the story flow,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. make predictions based on the title and the sections read,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the role of characters in the class reader. ● Learners are guided to read a section of a class reader and identify the main characters. ● In groups, learners are guided to discuss predictions made from the title and the sections read. ● Learners are guided to participate in a reader’s theatre and read portions of the class reader. ● Learners are guided to outline the things done by each character studied in the section. ● In pairs, learners are guided to discuss how the characters make the story flow. ● Learners are guided to write a summary about how the main characters make the story flow. 1.
